applicability.notes: M002 is instantiated with X=Eucl(k), d=a and s=A; D001 supplies the metric and Borel structures. Its nonempty-member cost agrees with D003 at every finite positive scale because a>0, including diameter zero; empty members cost zero. M003 and M004 use the same space and set and the nonnegative-real representative of a>0. Their strict dimension inequalities are precisely L1 and L2, respectively, and their conclusions are converted by F001. The supplied signatures impose no set-measurability condition. Routine background conditions are verified in the notes.

argument.notes: S001 compares identical finite-scale cover costs and correctly discards the additional infinite scale: its infimum is no larger than any finite-scale infimum. S002 applies the two critical-exponent premises; S003 obtains the converse bounds by contradiction and nonnegativity from D005. In S004 cover inclusion gives content and measure inequalities, and a finite positive intermediate exponent contradicts any strict reversal of dimensions, including an infinite larger dimension. In S005 image covers after intersection with A and inverse-image covers after intersection with g(A) preserve coverage and do not increase diameters; distance preservation supplies injectivity and equality of pairwise distances. The resulting two content inequalities imply equality at every scale and hence equality of suprema, without any exchange of limits. F003 and the same intermediate-exponent argument give equality of dimensions. Empty sets have zero positive-exponent contents, so F003 bounds their dimension by every positive real and nonnegativity makes it zero. Every N001 clause follows.

background_notes.fact: For a>0 and finite nonnegative real d, the extended nonnegative-real power of d agrees with the embedding of its real power d^a, including d=0. A finite or countably infinite family of sets with nonnegative costs can be indexed by N, using empty zero-cost members when padding is necessary, without changing its union or total cost.

grounds.reason: D003 uses countable covers and assigns empty members cost zero.
M002 uses N-indexed covers, nonnegative extended sums and zero empty-member cost.
The exponent is positive and admissible diameters at finite scale are finite.

background_notes.justification: At positive finite d both powers are defined by exp(a log d); at d=0 positivity of a gives zero in both conventions. Enumerate a countably infinite family bijectively, or list a finite family and pad with empties. Nonnegative sums are suprema of finite subsums, so reindexing or adding zero terms preserves the sum.

background_notes.fact: For extended nonnegative costs, infima and suprema preserve pointwise order. In particular, if each cover in a target admissible class yields a source admissible cover of no greater cost, then the source infimum is at most the target infimum; the corresponding inequality persists after taking the supremum over positive scales. A pointwise inequality between nonnegative summands implies the same inequality between their series.

grounds.reason: Contents are infima over cover costs, and H is their supremum over positive scales.
Under L3 each B-cover is an A-cover.

background_notes.justification: The source infimum is bounded above by each constructed cost and hence by each target cover cost; it is therefore a lower bound for all target costs and is at most their infimum. This remains valid for an empty admissible class, whose infimum is top. Suprema preserve pointwise order by their upper-bound characterization. Series inequalities follow from finite subsum inequalities and taking suprema. For v>0 the function d↦d^v on nonnegative reals is increasing (on positive arguments by increasing log and exp, and at zero by nonnegativity), so nonincreasing diameters give nonincreasing cover costs.

background_notes.fact: If 0≤p<q≤infinity in the extended nonnegative reals, there is a finite real v>0 with p<v<q. Consequently, two such extended values that have the same positive-exponent zero/infinity comparisons in F003 cannot be unequal.

grounds.reason: F003 supplies critical-exponent implications for every Euclidean set and every positive real exponent.
S004 assumes the strict dimension inequality to obtain a contradiction.

background_notes.justification: The smaller p must be finite. If q is finite choose v=(p+q)/2; if q=infinity choose v=p+1. These choices are finite and positive and satisfy both strict inequalities. For unequal dimensions, apply F003 at this v: the larger dimension has infinite measure and the smaller has zero measure, contradicting the inequality in S004 or equality in S005.
